title: Rochester organization celebrates Austin Steward Day - NewsBreak
text: ROCHESTER, N.Y. (WROC) — Wednesday is Austin Steward Day — a holiday to celebrate the legacy of the Rochester historical figure. Steward was one of Rochester’s first Black business owners and had a hand in building many important buildings in the city. He was also a freed slave and an abolitionist. In honor of Steward’s legacy, Community Justice Initiative is celebrating the holiday at the Arnett Library. During this celebration, they will hand out the Austin Steward Award to three members of the community who exemplify strong activism and business skills. Also at the celebration were storytellers and reenactments, vendors, a community town hall discussion, and free food. “Beautiful sight to see, especially being an advocate for the youth, extensively working in the community with the youth,” CJI co-builder Niya Shabazz said. “It’s important for them to be here and witness what unity looks like, getting knowledge from right here in these roots, you know, we have a lot of historical black history right here in Rochester.” And for a little history: Austin Steward escaped slavery in 1814, and made his way to Rochester. He published a memoir titled “Twenty-Two Years a Slave, and Forty Years a Freeman” in 1857. He passed in 1869, and was buried in Canandaigua.
